transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Nina (Redwood SE), Aisha (MapleBeam Head of Platform), Tommy (CTO), Rebecca (SRE)

Summary:
MapleBeam is evaluating Redwood for a user-facing personalization API. Primary asks: fast time-to-first-token (TTFT) for a PLG flow, free credits to prototype, and clarity on hosted vs dedicated fit given their multi-tenant privacy policy and expected QPS (~50-200 p50, bursts to 1k). Security and SSO are important but not blocking. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provision credits, share benchmark notebook and security artifacts, schedule a short technical run to validate latency and cost tradeoffs.

Topics: quickstart/PLG path, free credits and org setup, hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs (isolation, predictability), basic benchmark approach (batching, KV cache), SSO/SOC2 questions, rollout timing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, im Samir from Redwood, i know it's valentines day so appreciate the time, uh quick intros?
[00:04] Aisha: hi Aisha here, head of platform at MapleBeam, we own the inference layer and platform tooling
[00:07] Tommy: Tommy, CTO, product is pushing for a quick prototype they can enable in two weeks
[00:11] Rebecca: Rebecca, SRE lead, i'll be focusing on operational constraints and security review
[00:15] Nina: nina here, i'll cover the technical fit and runbook stuff, happy to dig into benchmarks
[00:20] Samir: great, quick agenda — we cover quickstart flow and credits, hosted/dedicated fit decisions, and then tech follow-up items, ok?
[00:25] Aisha: sounds good

[02:10] Samir: first Q — what's your must-have for TTFT, do you want api keys dropped into product for beta users?
[02:18] Aisha: yeah ideally we want something we can embed in the signup flow so a user gets a personalized suggestion on first session, goal is under 200ms p50 at prototype scale but we can tolerate 500ms p50 as long as p95 is under 1s, those are our rough numbers
[02:33] Tommy: to add, we expect low tokens per request — like 50 to 200 tokens — but need consistent tail latency
[02:40] Nina: ok that's helpful, for those numbers hosted Redwood API can hit that with small models and streaming disabled, and we can tune batching and KV cache to reduce cost. if you need guaranteed slices of GPU or predictable SLAs that's where Dedicated comes in

[04:05] Rebecca: question — we have some PII in prompts (hashed ids). how is data handled on hosted, are logs retained, can we purge?
[04:18] Samir: good call — hosted by default doesn't persist prompts beyond request logs we retain for 30 days, but we have options: dedicated or private to meet retention and KMS requirements. we also support customer-managed keys via K M S integrations for private deployments. i'll send the SOC 2 and dataflow doc after the call

[06:00] Aisha: what about SSO and org provisioning, we need SAML S S O and SCIM to onboard 12 engineers quickly
[06:12] Nina: we do SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for teams on paid tiers; for PLG quickstarts we can do invite-based orgs and then move to SSO during pilot. it's usually low friction — we have an admin console to manage API keys and roles

[08:15] Samir: credits — we typically provision free credits for proofs of concept, what's a realistic amount for you to validate p50/p95 under your expected load?
[08:25] Tommy: we can do with 30k tokens for initial prototypes but we'll need more to run concurrency tests, maybe 30k to 100k depending on the benchmarks
[08:35] Samir: ok we'll provision 30k to get you started and can top up for benchmarking runs; i'll follow up with the invite and credit allocation

[10:45] Nina: technical note — to measure tail latency you want to test with realistic prompt patterns. we'll give a simple Jupyter notebook that runs sequence length 512 and 128 tests, toggles batching, and shows cost per 1k tokens across hosted and dedicated profiles. Dedicated typically reduces latency variability at higher QPS because you get reserved GPUs and less noisy neighbors

[12:30] Rebecca: curious about KV cache — our personalization uses cached user context, is that supported on hosted? any risk with multi-tenancy?
[12:42] Nina: yes KV cache is supported. hosted runs cache in the serving layer with namespace isolation; it's ephemeral but safe for user-level context. for stricter isolation (regulatory) dedicated or private gives you physical separation and customer-managed cache configs

[15:00] Aisha: cost tradeoffs — can you ballpark hosted per-1k token vs dedicated reserved cost for smaller models? we want to compare cost to our current on-prem cost
[15:12] Samir: very rough rules: hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be cheaper at low usage. dedicated becomes cost efficient as you commit and get predictable throughput; Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quant to lower token costs. we'll include a short model-to-cost estimate in the follow-up doc.

[18:00] Tommy: timeline question — we have a product deadline in 5 weeks for a beta. can we realistically be in a hosted quickstart and then flip to dedicated later?
[18:12] Nina: yes that's a common path: start PLG on hosted to get TTFT and UX validated, then when traffic and predictability need increases, migrate traffic to Dedicated with the same API surface and model pins. rollouts and A/B via console are supported

[22:00] Rebecca: security checklist — SAML, SOC 2, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, and VPC peering for private deploys, do you have a single pkg or separate artifacts?
[22:15] Samir: we'll share a security pack (SOC 2 report, ISO summary, KMS integration guide, network diagrams). for private on-prem we have an ops package and checklist — i'll send links after the call

[25:45] Aisha: any gotchas with streaming or function calling that could impact TTFT? we may use a short response stream for UX
[25:58] Nina: streaming can add a small overhead but usually improves perceived latency. function-calling is supported; just note that streaming with small token counts may not be worth the overhead. we'll show tradeoffs in the notebook

[29:30] Tommy: competitor question — some teams prefer Anthropic for safety features, others like running local inference, how do you compare?
[29:42] Samir: we try to be agnostic with a curated catalog of compatible models; Redwood focuses on serving and economics — we let you choose model that balances safety and cost. for local inference you'd pick Private with on-prem runtime.

[32:00] Nina: for benchmarking we'll set up two profiles: hosted baseline and a lightweight dedicated profile (1 GPU of reserved capacity) and run the same workload in both to compare p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens

[34:10] Aisha: great. what do we need to share to get started?
[34:18] Samir: sample prompts, expected concurrency (even rough ballpark), authentication preference (SAML now or later), and which models you want to try. also point us at any compliance redlines (e.g., no logs persist longer than X)

[36:05] Rebecca: we'll gather that. one more operational — how are webhooks and retries handled on host? if we get throttled how will the client see it?
[36:17] Nina: we surface clear error codes and headers. rate-limiting returns 429 with retry-after, and the console shows throttling metrics. for Dedicated we can set higher quotas and dedicated burst capacity

[39:00] Samir: ok to recap: i'll provision 30k free credits and invite MapleBeam org, send pricing summary and security pack. nina will share benchmark notebook and runbook. Aisha will share prompt sets and QPS estimates. then we schedule a 30-min technical bench run next week.
[39:25] Aisha: sounds good, thanks everyone
[39:30] Tommy: thanks, appreciate the quick details
[39:35] Rebecca: thanks
[39:40] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with invites and docs

End of meeting.
